Sent through your circumvention tool. Where it connected is not shown, because you chose not to log it.
Your circumvention tool. Its traffic includes the traffic of the apps you send through it.
Traffic sent for an app shows under the app that sent it. Push messages come through Google Play services, and downloads through Android\'s download manager.
Watch does not see content. For encrypted traffic it sees the size, the place and the time, never what was sent.
Watch does not see what an app does on the phone, such as reading your contacts, files or photos. Only the sending shows.

Some apps cannot be told apart. Apps that share a number count together. A keyboard counts as in use while the screen is on. Your circumvention tool carries the traffic of the apps you send through it.

Watch sees nothing while another VPN is on, from apps you left out, or from a work profile, a private space or another user. It also sees nothing before the first unlock after a restart, or when traffic goes around the VPN. Traffic between apps on the phone never reaches it.
Sizes are what the apps sent and received through Watch. Android\'s data usage screen also counts headers and resent data, so it shows a little more.
\"With its notification\" means Android lets the app show one, not that you saw it. A channel you turned off still counts.

\"In use\" is what Android records of each app\'s screens. The feed left of the home screen on some phones counts as in the background. An app allowed to open screens from the background can look in use.
